Referral Note (outpatient therapist)

Mr. Varghese is a 28-year-old second-generation Indian American software engineer whom I see in individual therapy. He describes feeling different from other people for as long as he can remember, with ongoing difficulty in social situations and a strong preference for routine. He works full time and lives independently but has few close relationships. He was diagnosed with social anxiety in college and has had little benefit from treatment, and I am not confident that diagnosis accounts for his presentation. He is medically healthy and takes no medications. Referred for diagnostic clarification.

Behavioral Observations (on arrival)

Appearance: Casually dressed; appropriately groomed. Noise-cancelling headphones around his neck.

Behavior: Cooperative. Limited eye contact.

Speech: Monotone. Normal rate and volume.

Mood / Affect: Mood "fine." Affect restricted.

Thought / Perception: Thought process logical. No evidence of psychosis.

Cognition / Insight: Alert and oriented. Insight good; judgment intact.
